plan_a_advantages: Includes longer runs (up to 35km) which are more representative of trail running distances and build endurance.
Incorporates hill repeats, directly addressing a key challenge in trail running.
Includes a strength training session, important for injury prevention and power on trails.
Higher overall volume (435 minutes vs 348) allows for greater adaptation and development of trail-specific fitness.
plan_b_advantages: Focuses on higher-intensity interval and tempo work, which can improve speed and lactate threshold.
Lower overall volume (348 minutes) might be suitable for athletes with limited time or higher injury risk.
The interval session could improve running economy.
reasoning: Given the goal of becoming a faster trail runner, Plan A appears to be the better choice. Trail running demands a blend of aerobic endurance, hill strength, and the ability to sustain effort over varied terrain. Plan A incorporates longer runs with significant elevation gain, hill repeats, and a strength component, all of which are crucial for trail running performance. Plan B, while including interval and tempo sessions, lacks the sustained aerobic work and hill-specific training that are essential for trail running success.
